## Setup

Let $N$ be the total number of games. The match ends when one player reaches 21 wins, so $N = 21 + L$, where $L$ is the number of games the eventual winner lost. Let $p = 0.3$ (Frank wins a game) and $q = 0.7$ (Joe wins a game).

## Expected value as a sum

If Frank wins the match with exactly $k$ losses ($0 \le k \le 20$), the probability is $\binom{20+k}{k}p^{21}q^k$, and that gives $N = 21+k$ games. Symmetrically for Joe. So

$$E[N] = \sum_{k=0}^{20} (21+k)\binom{20+k}{k}\left[p^{21}q^k + q^{21}p^k\right].$$

Using $(21+k)\binom{20+k}{k} = 21\binom{21+k}{k}$, the Frank-wins part becomes

$$21\,p^{21}\sum_{k=0}^{20}\binom{21+k}{k}q^k = \frac{21}{p}\,P(Y\le 20),$$

where $Y \sim \text{NegBin}(22,p)$ counts Joe's wins before Frank's 22nd win. The event $Y \le 20$ means Frank gets at least 22 wins in the first 42 games. Symmetrically, the Joe-wins part is $\frac{21}{q}P(\text{Frank has} \le 20 \text{ wins in 42 games})$. Hence, with $X \sim \text{Bin}(42, 0.3)$,

$$E[N] = \frac{21}{0.3}P(X\ge 22) + \frac{21}{0.7}P(X\le 20) = 70\,P(X\ge 22) + 30\,P(X\le 20).$$

(Check: for first-to-1, this formula gives $p+q=1$, which is correct.)

## Numerical evaluation

Computing the binomial pmf at $k=21,22$ and summing the tail:

- $P(X=22) = \binom{42}{22}(0.3)^{22}(0.7)^{20} \approx 1.28652\times10^{-3}$
- $P(X=21) \approx 3.14482\times10^{-3}$
- $P(X\ge 22) \approx 1.99749\times10^{-3}$ (tail beyond 22 is included)
- $P(X\le 20) = 1 - P(X\ge 21) \approx 0.994858$

Then

$$E[N] \approx 70(0.00199749) + 30(0.994858) \approx 0.13982 + 29.84573 \approx 29.9856.$$

Equivalently, $E[N] = 30 + 40P(X\ge22) - 30P(X=21)$, which gives the same value.

This is plausible: Joe is a strong favourite, so the match typically ends near $21/0.7 = 30$ games.

ANSWER: ≈ 29.986
